evidence_gates.claim: On an attested native x86-64 host, compiles the pinned mimalloc C release source set with the exact recorded release flags, proves the selected x86-64 preprocessor mode and ELF identity, inventories globally defined mi_* symbols across the individual release objects, and separately inventories default-visible defined mi_* dynamic symbols in the linked shared object. This is evidence-only and does not claim public x86 crabc, libc, or ldso support or reuse AArch64 status.

On an attested native x86-64 host, consumes a fresh pinned normal-release C mode/object-symbol report and classifies all 194 distinct source-declared C functions by object and dynamic-symbol presence, while classifying 183 C/C++/macro/type/option source forms as not-an-object-symbol. It is selected-release source accounting only and does not claim declaration behavior, Rust implementation, public mi_* API, libc, loader, or public x86 runtime compatibility.

On an attested native x86-64 host, builds the pinned C normal-release shared object and compile-links five selected staged public C/C++ header forms against it, recording ELF identity for the shared object and every consumer. It proves staged pinned-header compile/linkability only; it does not prove CMake configuration or installation, consumer execution or behavior, Rust implementation, public x86 runtime support, or AArch64 status.
Builds and inspects the separately compiled, pinned mimalloc C oracle. It does not claim a Rust C-API adapter or public allocator support.

Compares the native direct Rust engine's configuration/layout, small-allocation trace, and 75-field fundamental-operation trace (including fixed no-padding mi_expand NULL/nonzero, fitting, oversize, and preservation cases plus checked mi_recalloc growth, zero-product, and overflow-preservation cases) against the selected pinned C release profile. It does not claim a C-API adapter, general lifecycle, or public allocator integration.

On an attested native x86-64 host, verifies the exact unfeatured normal Rust engine graph (including cpufeatures and no selected libc package), then builds the #![no_std] engine as a fresh release fat-LTO rlib and records its LLVM bitcode codegen member. Cargo resolution is lockfile-verified; a fresh bind-mounted cache may populate from the network with lockfile-selected packages. This is not a final linked ELF, not a staticlib/cdylib, and not a public allocator ABI, libc integration, or backend-promotion claim.

On an attested native x86-64 host, builds and audits the private prefixed Rust C test adapter, then runs the checked-in allocator fixture and 33 selected patched upstream API checks. It exposes no mi_* symbols and does not establish a public crabc allocator ABI or backend.

On an attested native x86-64 host, measures one shared C fixture through pinned C mimalloc and the private crabc_test_* adapter, including post-initialization live-set memory observations. It is bounded single-thread private-adapter evidence with no promotion threshold; it does not qualify general mimalloc performance, public mi_* behavior, libc integration, or a backend.
Proves the private compiler-TLS roots and direct x86-64 TLS access model; it does not prove process/thread lifecycle parity.

On an attested native x86-64 host, runs eight named private Rust lifecycle/concurrency lanes with 12 selected tests, including five finite Loom head-protocol models. It is not general process/thread lifecycle, client routing, abandonment/adoption, pthread callback, general fault-injection or misuse parity, or whole-allocator stress evidence.

On an attested native x86-64 host, differentially compares 25 address-independent values from exactly two live-owner mi_free publications by one quiescent pthread and the pinned private owner false collector, _mi_page_free_collect(page, false). It proves only source-specific owner-bit preservation, LIFO publication, exact used-count transition, and post-join detach/local-free merge. It is private engine evidence, not general remote-free routing or concurrent collection, abandonment, thread teardown, public mi_* API, libc integration, backend promotion, or AArch64 evidence.

On an attested native x86-64 host, differentially compares 28 address-independent values for one real small direct-cache page filled to its current capacity, one joined/quiescent pthread mi_free publication, and the owner direct-cache miss falling through the regular queue search to collect and reuse that exact block. It proves only this private small direct-page route; it is not general allocation/free routing or concurrent collection, abandonment, thread teardown, public mi_* API, libc integration, backend promotion, or AArch64 evidence.

On an attested native x86-64 host, differentially compares eight address-independent values for one private arena-backed mapped page with two same-page live blocks: source queue detachment and mapped abandonment, followed by one same-origin mi_free reclaim while the survivor keeps the page nonempty. It proves only this same-origin mapped reclaim and requeue transition; it is not general abandonment/adoption, cross-thread reclaim, public mi_* behavior, libc integration, backend promotion, or AArch64 evidence.

On an attested native x86-64 host, runs five named crate-private fault-injection state-preservation regressions covering selected Map, Commit, Unmap, and Decommit points. It does not establish general fault-injection or misuse parity, syscall interposition, lifecycle/stress coverage, C-oracle differential behavior, public mi_* behavior, libc integration, or a backend.
Exercises the allocator engine's selected x86-64 configuration, including its one 4 KiB base-page profile.

implementation_regressions.claim: Compiles and runs the crabc-core `%fs:0` thread-pointer implementation on native x86-64. This is an implementation regression, not independent C-oracle or allocator lifecycle evidence.

ledger_boundary.reason: Those checked-in ledgers encode AArch64 production API, adapter, dependency, and verification claims. The x86-64 adapter contract source-binds only the reviewed patch and selected C checks; it does not inherit their target, dependency, or public-API claims. Copying the remaining fields into an x86-64 file would falsely claim parity.

not_yet_covered_lanes.reason: The native private adapter is covered, but it exposes only crabc_test_* evidence symbols. It does not expose a public mi_* API or establish crabc-libc allocator integration on x86-64.

Eight bounded private Rust lifecycle/concurrency lanes (12 tests, including five finite Loom models), five bounded crate-private fault-injection state-preservation regressions, a separate 25-field native C/Rust quiescent live-owner remote-free protocol differential, and one 28-field real small direct-page remote-free/reuse differential are recorded, but general remote-free routing or concurrent collection, process/thread teardown, abandonment/adoption lifecycle, pthread callbacks, fault/misuse coverage, and stress remain incomplete allocator work.
This profile neither selects the Rust engine as a libc backend nor establishes public crabc x86-64 support.
Bounded native private-adapter timing and post-init live-memory measurements are recorded, but no whole-engine, lifecycle/concurrency, public-API, or backend performance qualification exists.

scope: A target-local evidence and implementation ledger for the pinned crabc-mimalloc engine on native Linux/x86-64 little-endian.
